questions.question: Who among the following wrote the popular Telugu patriotic song ‘Desamunu preminchumanna, manchi annadi penchumanna’ meaning ‘Love the nation, grow the goodness’?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Gurajada Apparao** wrote the popular Telugu patriotic song 'Desamunu preminchumanna, manchi annadi penchumanna' meaning 'Love the nation, grow the goodness'.
 
• Gurajada Apparao was a renowned Indian playwright, poet, and writer known for his contributions to Telugu literature.
 
• His works often focused on social reform and the promotion of national consciousness.
 
• The song 'Desamunu preminchumanna' is celebrated for its patriotic fervor and has inspired generations of Indians.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• He is also known for his famous play **Kanyasulkam**, which is considered one of the greatest works in Telugu literature.
 
• Apparao's literary works played a significant role in the cultural renaissance of Andhra Pradesh.
 
• His writings emphasized the importance of education, social justice, and national integration.

questions.question: In Kabaddi, a super tackle is when a raider is caught/self out/declared out with or less than how many defenders defending?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Three**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A super tackle in Kabaddi is when a raider is caught/self out/declared out with three or fewer defenders defending.
 
• This rule adds an extra point to the defending team’s score for successfully tackling the raider under these conditions.
 
• It is a strategic advantage for the defending team as it not only prevents the raider from scoring but also boosts their own score.
 
• Super tackles are crucial in turning the tide of the match, especially when the defending team is outnumbered.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Kabaddi is a contact team sport that originated in India and is popular in many South Asian countries.
 
• The game is played with two teams of seven players each, and the objective is for a single raider to tag members of the opposing team and return to their own half without being tackled.
 
• A match consists of two halves, typically 20 minutes each, with a 5-minute break in between.
 
• The sport requires a combination of strength, strategy, and agility, making it both exciting and challenging.

questions.question: ________ has called the Right to Constitutional Remedy as the ‘Soul of the Constitution’.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dr. BR Ambedkar**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dr. BR Ambedkar** has called the Right to Constitutional Remedy as the 'Soul of the Constitution'.
 
• The Right to Constitutional Remedy is enshrined in **Article 32** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It empowers citizens to approach the Supreme Court or High Courts to seek enforcement of other fundamental rights recognized by the Constitution.
 
• Dr. BR Ambedkar emphasized its importance, asserting that without this remedy, all other rights would be meaningless.
 
• This right ensures that the judiciary can act as a protector of the Constitution and the rights it guarantees.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 32** of the Indian Constitution provides the right to individuals to move to the Supreme Court for the enforcement of fundamental rights.
 
• It is termed the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution by Dr. BR Ambedkar because it provides a guaranteed remedy for the protection of fundamental rights.
 
• This article includes the issuance of writs such as habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto, and certiorari.
 
• It plays a crucial role in maintaining the rule of law and the protection of the rights of citizens against arbitrary actions of the state.
 
• The Supreme Court has the power to issue directions, orders, or writs for the enforcement of any of the rights conferred by Part III of the Constitution.

questions.question: Bali Yatra, is a traditional cultural festival of which state?

• The state has a diverse range of tribal communities, each with its own unique traditions and customs.
 
• Tourism plays a significant role in Odisha's economy, with attractions ranging from beaches to wildlife sanctuaries and historical monuments.

questions.question: Which type of soil is found on about 40% of the total area of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Alluvial soil**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Alluvial soil** is found on about 40% of the total area of India.
 
• This type of soil is primarily found in the plains of the northern and coastal regions of India.
 
• Alluvial soil is highly fertile and suitable for growing a variety of crops, including rice, wheat, sugarcane, and cotton.
 
• The soil is deposited by rivers and is rich in nutrients like potash, phosphoric acid, and lime.
 
• It supports extensive agricultural activities and is a significant contributor to India's agrarian economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Alluvial soil is divided into two types: **New alluvium (Khadar)** and **Old alluvium (Bhangar)**.
 
• **Khadar soil** is found in the floodplains of rivers and is renewed annually by fresh silt deposits.
 
• **Bhangar soil** is found on higher terraces and is older, with higher concentrations of clay and organic matter.
 
• These soils are especially predominant in the Indo-Gangetic Plain, which includes states like Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, and West Bengal.
 
• The fertility of alluvial soil makes it a crucial resource for India's food security and agricultural productivity.

questions.question: In which judgement did the Supreme Court extend the scope of Article 21 and observed that ‘the Right to education flows directly from the Right to life’?

options.text: Kharak Singh v State of UP
Malak Singh v State of Punjab
Neerja Choudhari v State of M. P
Mohini Jain v State of Karnataka

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mohini Jain v State of Karnataka**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Supreme Court of India, in the case of **Mohini Jain v State of Karnataka**, extended the scope of Article 21 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The judgement observed that the **Right to education flows directly from the Right to life**, which is guaranteed under Article 21.
 
• This landmark decision emphasized that the state is obligated to provide educational facilities to its citizens as a part of their fundamental rights.
 
• The ruling paved the way for subsequent decisions and legislations that strengthened the right to education in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 21** of the Indian Constitution states that "No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law."
 
• The interpretation of Article 21 has been broadened over the years to include various rights that are essential to the life and dignity of an individual.
 
• The **Right to Education Act**, 2009, which provides free and compulsory education to all children aged 6 to 14 years, was a significant step towards realizing the right recognized in the Mohini Jain case.
 
• The Constitution (Eighty-sixth Amendment) Act, 2002, also inserted Article 21A, explicitly making education a fundamental right for children in the specified age group.

questions.question: _____ at Market Price refers to the sum total of factor incomes earned by residents of a country during an accounting year including net indirect taxes.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Net National Product (NNP)**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Net National Product (NNP)** at Market Price refers to the sum total of factor incomes earned by residents of a country during an accounting year including net indirect taxes.
 
• It is derived by subtracting depreciation from Gross National Product (GNP).
 
• It represents the net value of goods and services produced by the residents of a country.
 
• NNP is an important indicator of the economic health of a country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The calculation of NNP takes into account the depreciation of capital assets, making it a more accurate measure of economic performance than Gross National Product (GNP).
 
• Net National Product (NNP) can be used to gauge the standard of living within a country, as it reflects the actual income available to the residents.
 
• It is also used for international comparisons of economic performance.
 
• Depreciation represents the wear and tear on the capital stock, which is why it is deducted from the Gross National Product to arrive at the Net National Product.
 
• Higher NNP indicates a higher level of economic activity and prosperity within a country.

questions.concept: India under East India Company’s Rule
questions.question: Which of the following was a feature of the Indian economy before British rule?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Independent economy.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Independent economy** was a major feature of Indian economy before British rule.
 
• Indian economy was** independent and self-sufficient** before British rule, consisting of various types of **agriculture, handicrafts, and trade.**
 
• India was a major exporter of **various textiles, spices, and other products**, making it a strong and prosperous economy.
 
• Local cottage **industries and handicraft industries** were the backbone of the Indian economy, providing employment in rural and urban areas.
 
• With the advent of British rule, the structure of the Indian economy underwent **significant changes, **making it dependent and vulnerable.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• During British rule, the Indian economy was **exploited **and restructured to suit British economic interests.
 
• Many **local industries **and **handicrafts **were destroyed or weakened, leading to increased** poverty and unemployment.**
 
• Indian economy became overly dependent on** agriculture,** and farmers were forced to cultivate cash crops, leading to food crisis.
 
• During this period, the development of **manufacturing and industry** in the Indian economy was hampered, and the overall economic condition of the country weakened.

• Observation of Cygnus is best in the northern hemisphere during the late evening hours of summer and early fall.

questions.question: In which year did Eric A. Cornell, Wolfgang Ketterle and Carl E. Wieman receive the Nobel Prize in Physics for the achieving 'Bose-Einstein condensation in dilute gases of alkali atoms'?

• Eric A. Cornell and Carl E. Wieman conducted their research at the University of Colorado, while Wolfgang Ketterle conducted his research at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT).

questions.question: How many countries participated in the first Asian Games held in 1951?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**11**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **11 countries** participated in the first Asian Games held in 1951.
 
• The first Asian Games were hosted by **New Delhi, India** from March 4 to March 11, 1951.
 
• The participating countries were Afghanistan, Burma (Myanmar), Ceylon (Sri Lanka), India, Indonesia, Iran, Japan, Nepal, the Philippines, Singapore, and Thailand.
 
• The Asian Games, also known as Asiad, are a multi-sport event held every four years among athletes from all over Asia.
 
• The event is organized by the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA) and is recognized by the International Olympic Committee (IOC).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The idea of the Asian Games was initiated by India's first Prime Minister, **Jawaharlal Nehru**, and the Asian Games Federation was formed to organize the games.
 
• The first Asian Games featured six sports: athletics, aquatics (swimming, diving, water polo), basketball, cycling, football, and weightlifting.
 
• Since the inaugural event in 1951, the Asian Games have grown significantly in size and scope, with more countries and sports being added over the years.
 
• The Asian Games are considered the second-largest multi-sport event after the Olympic Games.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles was amended by The Constitution Fiftieth Amendment Act, 1984?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 33**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Constitution Fiftieth Amendment Act, 1984, amended **Article 33** of the Constitution of India.
 
• **Article 33** empowers the Parliament to restrict or abrogate the application of fundamental rights to the armed forces, paramilitary forces, police forces, intelligence agencies, and similar services.
 
• This amendment was aimed at ensuring proper discharge of duties and maintaining discipline among these forces.
 
• The amendment allows the government to impose necessary restrictions to maintain public order and national security.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Constitution of India** was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949** and **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written** constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**
 
• The **Seventh Schedule** of the Constitution contains three lists which delineate the subjects under the **Union, State, and Concurrent lists**.
 
• Amendments to the Constitution can be made through a process outlined in **Article 368**.
 
• Article 33 is crucial for maintaining discipline and proper functioning of the armed forces and other similar services by allowing necessary restrictions on fundamental rights.

questions.question: When did the first War of Indian Independence (Sepoy Mutiny) start?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1857**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The first War of Indian Independence, also known as the Sepoy Mutiny, started in the year **1857**.
 
• This uprising was a major, but ultimately unsuccessful, rebellion against the British East India Company's rule in India.
 
• The revolt began on May 10, 1857, in the town of Meerut and soon spread to other parts of India.
 
• Key figures in the rebellion included Rani Lakshmibai of Jhansi, Bahadur Shah Zafar, and Tantia Tope, among others.
 
• The revolt was fueled by various factors including political, economic, social, and military grievances against the British rule.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Sepoy Mutiny marked the end of the rule of the British East India Company and led to the direct control of India by the British Crown.
 
• This event is considered a significant precursor to the later movements for Indian independence.
 
• The rebellion highlighted the widespread discontent and laid the foundation for future freedom struggles.
 
• After the revolt, the British implemented various reforms to placate the Indian populace and prevent further uprisings.
